parsed.rationale: Two computed properties in the same `Wallpaper` package — `ProcessInfo.ThermalState.description` in the sample-app's `DebugHUD.swift` (line 237) and `PerformanceControls.thermalStateLabel` in `PerformanceControls.swift` (line 152) — share near-identical logic for converting a `ProcessInfo.ThermalState` value to a human-readable string (Jaccard 0.75). The canonical home for this logic is a single extension on `ProcessInfo.ThermalState` placed in the main `Wallpaper` source tree (e.g., `Shared/Wallpaper/Sources/Wallpaper/DebugUI/ThermalState+Description.swift`), which both the production `PerformanceControls` and the sample-app `DebugHUD` can then consume. Because one participant is `is_sample_app: true` and the other is production code, the duplication is not intentional mirroring — the sample app is simply re-implementing something the library should already expose.
